jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Surprise
jokes.joke: I hired a party planner who said, “Do you trust me?” Apparently her big prank was telling all my guests the party started two hours earlier. By the time I arrived, they’d eaten, sung “Happy Birthday,” and gone home. Technically, she delivered exactly what I paid for: a surprise party where I was the surprise.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Surprise Party Physics
jokes.joke: I planned my husband's fortieth as a surprise. We hid in the dark, waiting. He walks in, I jump out screaming, and he punches me on pure instinct. Full haymaker. So now the surprise is on me, in urgent care, telling a nurse 'birthday party' while she writes down 'domestic incident' and looks at me like I'm the one lying about the balloons.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Cover Charge
jokes.joke: Being a professional party planner ruins your ability to pull a simple prank. I tried setting up the classic bucket of water over the door to soak my husband. But my professional instincts took over. By the time he walked through, it was San Pellegrino with a lemon twist, and I charged him a fifty-dollar cover just to get into our own bathroom.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Anniversary Overdraft
jokes.joke: I wanted to do something extravagant for our anniversary, so I staged a huge prank. Fake lottery win, actors with a giant check, balloons, champagne—the whole production. She was so excited she quit her job on the spot. The prank went wrong the next morning when the bank called. Now the only extravagant thing in our life is the size of the overdraft.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Creek Catastrophe
jokes.joke: I tried to pull a harmless prank on my buddy during our creek hike—just a little splash to scare him. But I slipped, windmilled like a malfunctioning lawn ornament, and landed face-first in the water. He didn’t even help me up. He just said, “Man, if that was the prank, the creek already got you back.”

The upscale-prank transformation is unexpected and coherent; San Pellegrino and the bathroom cover charge provide good escalating specifics.
Clear premise and structure, but fake-lottery disaster is familiar and the overdraft ending is only loosely connected to the strongest comic consequence.
Understandable slapstick with clean first-person form, but the fall is predictable and the final line mostly explains the reversal rather than adding a stronger turn.
Clean setup, tight escalation, and a solid pun-payoff ('I was the surprise'); works but the twist is telegraphed a beat early.
Vivid professional-deformation angle, concrete image (San Pellegrino, lemon twist) and a sharp closing overcharge line; best-constructed of the batch.

Nice 'malfunctioning lawn ornament' image, but the prankster-gets-pranked outcome is predictable and the closer lands soft.
Competent logic and clean rhythm, but the final line lands more like an intellectual semantic tidy-up than a punchy laugh.
